course.title: Figma — Complete Deep Design Course
course.description: A Figma-specific, beginner-to-advanced course with detailed concepts, visual examples, practical design exercises, dedicated tasks, validation and a complete learning-platform capstone.
course.curriculumPolicy: Module and lesson counts are determined by the concepts required to learn the subject properly; no fixed cross-design template is imposed.
prerequisites: No prior professional design experience required
learningOutcomes: Design clear and consistent interfaces or user experiences.
Use evidence and structured reasoning for design decisions.
Build a complete learning-platform design case study.

modules.title: Figma Foundations
modules.description: Figma interface, files, pages, frames, layers and the core mental model for collaborative design.

lessons.title: Figma Foundations
lessons.description: Figma interface, files, pages, frames, layers and the core mental model for collaborative design.
learningObjectives: Apply the concept to a realistic product.
Explain the reasoning behind design decisions.

notes.text: Figma interface, files, pages, frames, layers and the core mental model for collaborative design.
Learn figma foundations by understanding the user's goal first, then the design principle, then a concrete interface/flow example, and finally how to validate whether the design actually helps users.

Figma Foundations directly affects how easily students can discover courses, understand lessons, complete tasks and recover from mistakes. Good design is not decoration; it reduces friction and improves comprehension.

notes.caption: Add a clear design/UX diagram showing the concept and its application to the learning platform.

items: Start from a real user goal.
Make hierarchy and next actions clear.
Reduce unnecessary cognitive load.
Design normal, loading, empty, error and success states.
Validate decisions with users or structured review.

notes.code:
Scenario: Create the foundation file for a learning-platform redesign.

Design flow: identify user/task -> prioritize information -> choose pattern -> design -> validate -> iterate.

items: Identify the user and task.
Identify the most important information.
Choose hierarchy and interaction pattern.
Design the happy path.
Design error/empty/loading states.
Check accessibility and responsive behavior.
Validate and iterate.
Designing for aesthetics before understanding the task.
Using inconsistent spacing or component behavior.
Hiding important information behind unnecessary interactions.
Ignoring empty/error states.
Assuming desktop design automatically works on mobile.
Skipping accessibility and usability validation.
Use consistent design tokens and components.
Keep primary actions obvious.
Use progressive disclosure for complex information.
Write clear labels and feedback.
Design for accessibility from the beginning.
Validate designs with realistic user tasks.
I can explain Figma Foundations in my own words.
I can apply the principle to a learning-platform screen/flow.
I can explain why my design decision helps the user.
I can identify a usability/accessibility risk.
I can describe how I would validate the design.

notes.text: Create a complete responsive product design with design system, components, prototypes, states, accessibility and developer handoff.

Learn capstone: figma learning platform by understanding the user's goal first, then the design principle, then a concrete interface/flow example, and finally how to validate whether the design actually helps users.

Capstone: Figma Learning Platform directly affects how easily students can discover courses, understand lessons, complete tasks and recover from mistakes. Good design is not decoration; it reduces friction and improves comprehension.

notes.alt: Figma Capstone: Figma Learning Platform visual
notes.caption: Add a clear design/UX diagram showing the concept and its application to the learning platform.

items: Start from a real user goal.
Make hierarchy and next actions clear.
Reduce unnecessary cognitive load.
Design normal, loading, empty, error and success states.
Validate decisions with users or structured review.

notes.code:
Scenario: Design the complete student learning experience in Figma.

Design flow: identify user/task -> prioritize information -> choose pattern -> design -> validate -> iterate.

items: Identify the user and task.
Identify the most important information.
Choose hierarchy and interaction pattern.
Design the happy path.
Design error/empty/loading states.
Check accessibility and responsive behavior.
Validate and iterate.
Designing for aesthetics before understanding the task.
Using inconsistent spacing or component behavior.
Hiding important information behind unnecessary interactions.
Ignoring empty/error states.
Assuming desktop design automatically works on mobile.
Skipping accessibility and usability validation.
Use consistent design tokens and components.
Keep primary actions obvious.
Use progressive disclosure for complex information.
Write clear labels and feedback.
Design for accessibility from the beginning.
Validate designs with realistic user tasks.
I can explain Capstone: Figma Learning Platform in my own words.
I can apply the principle to a learning-platform screen/flow.
I can explain why my design decision helps the user.
I can identify a usability/accessibility risk.
I can describe how I would validate the design.
